# `aitbc system env-names`

List environment variable NAMES declared in a service's env files. Reads the unit's full ``EnvironmentFiles`` list via ``systemctl show`` so drop-in files are included. Names only — values and ``Environment=`` inline assignments are never printed. ``--process`` switches the source to the running process environment (``/proc/<MainPID>/environ``) — the only place variables set outside any ``EnvironmentFile`` (e.g. injected by a drop-in ``Environment=`` or a wrapper) show up. Still names only unless ``--value`` picks ONE non-deny-listed name.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc system env-names [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--service` | text | — | yes | Unit name (with or without the aitbc- prefix/.service suffix) |
| `--names` | text (multiple) | — | no | Report only whether each named variable is set (repeatable) |
| `--process` | flag | `false` | no | Read the running process environment via /proc/<MainPID>/environ — names only — instead of the declared env files; combined output flags declared_only/process_only drift |
| `--value` | text | — | no | Print the value of ONE named variable from the process environment (requires --process; the deny-list and length cap below apply — a refusal names the rule, never the value) |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc system env-names --service <service>
```
